title: DBFG-Net identifies cognitive impairment in chronic kidney disease from MRI features
summary: In a discovery cohort of 342 patients with CKD (177 with cognitive impairment, 165 without) and 58 matched controls, MRI features from T1-weighted imaging, arterial spin labeling and quantitative susceptibility mapping showing both stage-related trends and cognition-related discrimination were selected to train a Dual-Branch Feature-Gated Network. It reached AUC 0.942 in the discovery cohort and 0.902 and 0.926 in two external validation cohorts. Discriminative features were structural and susceptibility measures, not cerebral blood flow. Retrospective imaging study.
ai_technology: Dual-Branch Feature-Gated Network (DBFG-Net) deep model on selected multimodal MRI features
